record.paper_title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
record.original_question: In the non-bipartite regular multigraph setting of the source, let omega(k,n,r) denote the minimum number of k-matchings in the relevant r-regular multigraph class. For fixed r >= 2 and fixed density p in (0,2/3), does omega(k,n,r) grow exponentially in n for every integer k in the interval [pn, 2n/3], and what are sharp or useful lower bounds for that exponential growth rate?

evidence.quote: It is natural to conjecture that for any p ∈ (0, 2/3) and an integer k ∈ [pn, 2n/3] ω(k, n, r) has an exponential growth in n for a fixed r ≥ 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an integer $r \geq 2$, let $\mathcal{G}(n,r)$ denote the class of $r$-regular multigraphs on $n$ vertices (with $rn$ even, allowing parallel edges but no loops). A $k$-matching in a multigraph is a set of $k$ pairwise vertex-disjoint edges. For integers $k$ with $0 \leq k \leq n/2$, define
$$\omega(k,n,r) = \min_{G \in \mathcal{G}(n,r)} m_k(G),$$
where $m_k(G)$ is the number of $k$-matchings in $G$.

Fix $r \geq 2$ and a real number $p \in (0, 2/3)$. Prove or disprove: there exists a constant $c = c(p,r) > 1$ such that for every integer $k$ with $pn \leq k \leq 2n/3$,
$$\omega(k,n,r) \geq c^{n}$$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Moreover, determine sharp (or useful) lower bounds on the exponential growth rate $\liminf_{n\to\infty} \omega(k,n,r)^{1/n}$ as a function of $r$ and the density $k/n$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not find a definitive resolution of this conjecture about exponential growth of the minimum number of k-matchings in r-regular multigraphs for densities k/n in (0,2/3). Related results exist on perfect matchings and matchings at density 1/2 in regular graphs, but the specific conjecture for the interval [pn, 2n/3] does not appear to be resolved in the literature retrievable through search.

status_evidence.title: Perfect matchings in Claw-free Cubic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Every bipartite cubic n-vertex graph has at least 6(4/3)^(n/2−3) perfect matchings.
status_evidence.claim: Related exponential lower bounds are known for perfect matchings in cubic graphs, but not for the full density range below 2/3 considered here.

status_evidence.title: Results and open problems in matchings in regular graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem set; the density-(0,2/3) exponential growth conjecture is stated as natural to conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is presented as a conjecture without a proof.
